submission.justification: Radiator-R3 at 3 cm gives the highest pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c among the candidates and thicknesses tested: 4.645 sigma from the thickness scan, versus a best of 3.824 for R1 (at 2 cm) and 2.963 for R2 (at 3 cm). R3 is the best option at every thickness from 1 to 6 cm, and 3 cm is its peak. The simulation summary gives 4.6 sigma for R3 at 3 cm, 3.8 for R1 and 2.9 for R2, which agrees with the scan for R3 and R2 but is about 0.1 sigma higher than the scan for R1 (3.703 at 3 cm). The ranking is unchanged either way. However, the hard transparency constraint is NOT verified. The recorded results contain no 10-year humidity-ageing transparency measurement for any candidate, and candidate_specs.md was not among the results I was given. This recommendation is therefore conditional: the transparency loss of R3 after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing must be confirmed to be at most 10% before the radiator is committed, because it cannot be replaced during the run. If R3 fails that check, the choice must be revisited; I cannot certify it from the available data.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing must not exceed 10% (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No ageing or transparency measurement appears in the recorded results, and candidate_specs.md was not provided. Compliance for R3 cannot be confirmed and must be verified before use.
Selected thickness is 3 cm, within the 1-6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 3 cm gives 4.645 sigma (scan) / 4.6 sigma (simulation summary), the highest of all radiator and thickness combinations tested (R1 best 3.824, R2 best 2.963).

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness
requirements.evidence: This submission contains one radiator (Radiator-R3) and one thickness (3 cm).
